newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan tenders to sell Jul-Dec 3.0-pct fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan tenders to sell Jul-Dec 3.0-pct fuel oil.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a term tender to sell up to 180,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil for lifting between second half July and end December, a CPC source said on Thursday.
The tender offers four to six 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent sulphur, 180-centistoke grade fuel oil, on a free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis.
The tender closes on June 25 and bids will be valid for two days, the source said. The award will be on a floating price basis to Singapore spot quotes.
In its last term tender for January-June 1997 liftings, CPC sold four to six 30,000-tonne cargoes of high sulphur fuel oil at a $3.50-$4.00 per tonne premium to Singapore spot quotes, fob Kaohsiung.
CPC started exporting fuel oil on a six-monthly term basis by tender since early this year.
CPC recently sold by spot tender two 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for first half July delivery at around $100.50 per tonne on, fob Kaohsiung.
